item.title: Bangladesh opt to bat after winning toss against Afghanistan in Abu Dhabi Test
item.description:
Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto won the toss and elected to bat against Afghanistan in the one-off Test at the Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi on Friday.

Shanto said the pitch was quite dry and the weather was hot, leading him to believe that batting in the second innings would be more difficult.

Bangladesh have named an 11-man side featuring Shadman Islam, Tanzid Hasan, Mominul Haque, Najmul Hossain Shanto (captain), Mushfiqur Rahim, Litton Das (wicketkeeper), Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Nayeem Hasan, Hasan Mahmud, Taijul Islam and Ebadot Hossain.

Afghanistan’s side features Abdul Malik, Sediqullah Atal, Rahmat Shah (captain), Hashmatullah Shahidi, Ikram Alikhil (wicketkeeper), Zia-ur-Rehman, Shahidullah Kamal, Yamin Ahmadzai, Qais Ahmad, Mohammad Saleem Safi and Ismat Alam.

The match is Bangladesh’s first Test at a neutral venue.

The fixture is also significant for Afghanistan’s Test ranking prospects. Under the ICC’s criteria, a team must play at least eight Tests over a three-year period to be included in the Test rankings. This match is Afghanistan’s sixth Test during the period, meaning they need to play two more to qualify for the rankings.

Although Afghanistan are still relatively inexperienced in Test cricket, Bangladesh cannot afford to underestimate them.

item.title: India deploys thousands of police ahead of election protest
item.description:
INDIA-POLITICS-DEMONSTRATION

Thousands of police were deployed across the Indian capital on Friday, a day before planned protests to demand the election commission chief step down over alleged voter-roll irregularities.

Demonstrations have erupted this month over the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) “special intensive revision” of electoral rolls, which the commission says is intended to remove duplicate and ineligible voters.

Opposition parties and critics allege the exercise could disenfranchise voters to the benefit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

A wave of street protests, including in New Delhi, have attracted key leaders from India’s main opposition Congress party, including Rahul Gandhi, who was briefly detained during rallies this week.

Protesters, including from the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement, are calling for mass rallies in New Delhi on Saturday.

Gandhi, the leader of the opposition in parliament, and other opposition leaders are expected to meet President Droupadi Murmu later Friday to complain about ECI chief Gyanesh Kumar.

The ECI, India’s constitutional body responsible for conducting elections, has rejected allegations of wrongdoing.

More than 20,000 police and paramilitary officers have been deployed in the capital ahead of the protest, the Press Trust of India news agency reported.

Yellow metal barricades have sprung up across key roads in the city centre, restricting access to the government-designated protest site of Jantar Mantar, AFP reporters saw.

Police have not authorised rallies at the site.

The Cockroach Janta Party emerged online in May as a satirical political movement, and led protests at Jantar Mantar—which succeeded in a campaign to oust the then education minister.

The CJP has called for a “mass mobilisation” in New Delhi on Saturday, including an intended march to Jantar Mantar.

The movement has claimed that its volunteers and supporters were being detained by police ahead of the planned demonstration—allegations police did not respond to.

“Delhi police is working like the BJP’s private militia,” CJP activist Saurav Das said in a post on social media.

item.title: 252 detained in one night in anti-teenage gang drive in Cumilla
item.description:
Police detained 252 people in a single night during an operation against teenage gangs in Cumilla. The drive was conducted from Thursday evening until Friday morning by police from all 18 police stations in the district, in coordination with the Detective Branch (DB). However, police did not provide a breakdown of how many people were detained from each police station.

Additional Superintendent of Police Lutfur Rahman, the district police’s media officer, confirmed the information to Prothom Alo on Friday morning.

According to police, the operation targeted locations in different police station areas of the district where teenage gangs were active. Members of various district police units and the DB took part, along with senior police officials.

Crime continues in Cumilla despite crackdown as teen gang names appear on walls

Lutfur Rahman said the drive was conducted under the direction of Superintendent of Police Mohammad Anisuzzaman as part of ongoing operations against teenage gangs.

The authorities were verifying whether those detained were involved in criminal activities. Necessary legal action would be taken after the verification, he added.

The police official said regular drives were being conducted to prevent teenagers from becoming involved in crime. He added that the authorities were also monitoring the operations to ensure that no innocent person was harassed in the name of enforcement.

254 held in fresh crackdown on teen gangs in Cumilla, including Ratan Group's 'no. 2'

Earlier, on 23 September, an operation against teenage gangs was launched jointly by police from Cumilla’s 18 police stations and the DB. In the latest, fifth phase of the drive, conducted on the night of 2 October, police detained 370 people.

Of them, 279 were released into their families’ custody after signing undertakings, while legal action was taken against the remaining 91. During that operation, four people were arrested, including Imran Hossain, alias Ratan, leader of the notorious teenage gang known as the ‘Ratan Group’ or ‘R Squad’.

According to previous police figures, a total of 2,042 people had been detained in the first five phases of the operation. Following verification, 1,409 were released into their families’ custody after signing undertakings. Legal action was taken against the others based on allegations and information about their involvement in criminal activities.

Cumilla police of 18 police stations conduct anti-teen gang raids, detain 624 people

Police intensified the drive against teenage gangs in the district following the murder of Ishayat Shahriar Apratim, a Class VII student and son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor in the Department of Bangla at Cumilla University.

After he went missing on 18 September, his body was recovered the following day from a wooded area in the Lalmai hills in the Sananda area of Sadar South upazila. The incident prompted calls for stronger action to curb teenage gang activities and prevent juvenile crime.

Police said decisions regarding those detained were being made after checking information about their alleged links to teenage gangs, involvement in drug-related activities and other cases, as well as outstanding arrest warrants. Such operations would continue to prevent juvenile crime, they added.

item.title: Land minister seats Rajshahi Medical University VC in his office, says ‘miscreants have no political identity’
item.description:
Land Minister Mizanur Rahman Minu seated Rajshahi Medical University Vice-Chancellor Professor Jawadul Haque in his office chair on Thursday night. He visited the university’s temporary campus at around 9:00 pm and accompanied the vice-chancellor to his office.

Condemning the incident involving the vice-chancellor, the land minister said, “Those who behaved in this unfortunate manner are miscreants. They have no political identity. They are enemies of society.”

The minister added that no kind of disorder would be allowed in Rajshahi. Those involved in the incident would face legal action, he said, adding that the administration had been instructed to file cases against them and bring them to justice.

Addressing the vice-chancellor, the minister said, “Stay strong. We must take Rajshahi forward.”

On Tuesday, Vice-Chancellor Jawadul Haque was allegedly harassed and forced to sign a document at the temporary office of Rajshahi Medical University. At a press conference that afternoon, he said a group of 20 to 25 people had entered his room and asked him to sign a document without allowing him to read it. Fearing physical assault if he refused, he signed it. He believed the document was a resignation letter.

The vice-chancellor’s personal assistant and section officer (finance), Mohammad Nazmul Hossain, was also allegedly assaulted when he tried to intervene. The vice-chancellor and his assistant were subsequently forced out of the office. The vice-chancellor also alleged that the CPU of an office computer, CCTV equipment and other items had been removed, and that several university offices had been locked.

On Tuesday night, Nazmul Hossain filed a case with Rajpara Police Station over the incident. The case names 50 to 60 unidentified people as accused and includes allegations of obstructing government work, theft of equipment and vandalism. Police said they were identifying those involved by analysing video footage and photographs. Three people have been arrested in connection with the incident.

On Thursday morning, BNP and its affiliated organisations’ leaders and activists brought the vice-chancellor from his home in the Upashahar area to the university’s temporary campus. At around 11:15 am, the lock on his office was opened in the presence of Arif Hossain, an executive magistrate of the district administration. Later that night, the land minister visited the campus and seated the vice-chancellor in his office chair.

During the visit, Minister Mizanur Rahman also outlined plans for the university’s development. He said four major projects for the university were nearing approval, including one that received approval at a cabinet committee meeting on Thursday. He expressed hope that implementation of the projects would expand the university’s activities.

Urging patients and their relatives to treat physicians well, the minister said a physician could not attend to a large number of patients in a limited amount of time. It was therefore inappropriate to place unnecessary pressure on physicians. He also stressed the importance of planting more trees on the university campus and around the hospital.

Mohammad Shafiqul Haque Milan, a member of parliament for Rajshahi-3 (Paba-Mohanpur), said that if anyone attempted wrongdoing at the university in future, legal action should be taken regardless of their political affiliation. Being associated with a political party did not place anyone above the law, he added.

After taking his seat, Vice-Chancellor Jawadul Haque said that immediately after the incident, he had informed the land minister, local elected representatives, the health minister, the secretary and other relevant officials. They had all assured him of their support.

Those present included Rajshahi City Corporation Administrator Mahfujur Rahman Riton, Rajshahi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Abul Kalam Azad, Rajshahi Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mohammad Fayezul Kabir, metropolitan Jubo Dal convener Shariful Islam and metropolitan Chhatra Dal member secretary Imdadul Haque, among others.

item.title: Three women barred from travelling abroad describe what happened at the airport
item.description:
Three women have alleged that immigration police at the airport called their parents to ask about their travel plans and professions, and made “indecent” remarks about their clothing, financial means and personal matters.

One of the women said an immigration police officer told her that unmarried women were not allowed to travel abroad alone.

The three bachelor women, who were prevented from travelling abroad, made these statements to the police on Thursday. On 8 August, they went to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport with valid passports, visas or entry permits, and air tickets to travel to Nepal. However, they were stopped from travelling.

In response, they lodged a complaint with the additional inspector general of police on 30 August, seeking an investigation and action against those involved. After receiving no response, the three women filed a writ petition with the High Court.

Following an initial hearing on the petition, the court issued a rule and an order on 29 September, directing the authorities to dispose of the complaint the women had submitted to the additional inspector general of police.

Ishrat Hasan, the lawyer representing the three women, told Prothom Alo that, following the High Court order, the women were served notices asking them to appear on Thursday to give statements and be questioned as part of the process of disposing of their complaint.

A three-member committee has been formed to investigate the allegations. The women were questioned at the relevant office in Rajarbagh. They gave statements, and the recording of statement and questioning lasted around six hours.

'They were travelling to Nepal with their families’ consent’

One of the women stated in her testimony that she had been associated with the Bangladesh International Mediation Society (BIMS), an organisation working in mediation, since 2025. She said they planned to visit Nepal because BIMS had a representative there. They prepared for the trip after obtaining their families’ consent.

She said they were taken to an office while heading towards the terminal after collecting their boarding passes. She alleged that they were subjected to inappropriate behaviour from the outset. Officers made various offensive remarks about the photograph on her student ID card. Because the photograph showed her wearing a hijab, one officer allegedly said, “You dress differently at different times.”

The officer then called her father to ask about her travel plans. According to her statement, he told her father, “Keep track of what your daughter does. How can a farmer’s daughter afford to travel abroad?”

The young woman said she left the office afterwards. She alleged that the incident left her father traumatised. Subsequently, on 17 August, her father was involved in an accident and later died.

‘You are being stopped because you are not married’

Another woman stated that she had been working as a trainer and treasurer at BIMS since 2023. According to her account, she went to the airport on 8 August with two colleagues to travel to Nepal.

After collecting their boarding passes, they entered the terminal and submitted their passports and other documents for verification at a desk. They were then moved to an adjacent desk before all three women were taken to an office.

She said the police officers in the office kept her to one side and questioned the other two women. At one point, an officer called the father of one of the women and asked her to step outside.

The woman alleged that they had valid travel documents, but officers asked irrelevant questions without properly checking them. She also said officers made inappropriate remarks after seeing the details of a Nepali person in their hotel booking.

Later, a police officer called out their names. The women thought this meant they would finally be allowed to travel. She asked the officer where they were being taken. He replied that the three of them would be escorted out through the arrivals terminal.

When they asked why they were being sent out, the officer allegedly said they were not being allowed to travel because they were unmarried.

The woman said they were not given any written document when they were escorted out. Even outside, she repeatedly insisted that they would not leave the terminal premises. The officer then allegedly warned them that they would face problems if they stayed there.

‘Offensive remarks were made’

A third woman, who also works at BIMS, stated that she had entered the terminal on 8 August after following the required procedures and collecting her boarding pass. She was then taken from the terminal to an office, where officers asked to see her student ID card and told her to call her university’s dean.

She questioned whether it was appropriate to call the dean. An officer present then told her that he could contact his own superior if necessary, and asked why she could not call the dean.

The woman stated that she had travelled to the airport with all the required valid documents, including her boarding pass, passport, hotel booking and dollar endorsement. She alleged that officers questioned the source of the money for her trip and made offensive remarks. The police later retained her passport.

She further alleged that the officers called their parents on mobile phones to ask whether they knew their daughters were travelling abroad. They also asked about the women’s professions. According to her statement, the officers made various offensive remarks about their clothing and passports.

Questions asked during police questioning

On Thursday, the three women were asked whether they had received an invitation to meet Nepal’s chief justice. They replied that their purpose was to travel. As BIMS has a branch in Nepal, they had informally discussed meeting Nepal’s chief justice and attending a dinner with him through Simran, the local coordinator, during their visit.

Asked whether they had hotel bookings in Nepal and return tickets, the three women said they did.

They were also asked whether they had no-objection certificates (NOCs) from the organisations where they were interning. The women replied that NOCs were not required in their cases.

item.title: LPG shortage persists in market, prices remain high
item.description:
The supply shortage of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) has not eased in the market despite a price adjustment. Distributors say only six companies are supplying LPG regularly, but even they are unable to provide enough to meet demand. The price of the most widely used 12kg LPG cylinder is still Tk 500–600 higher than the official price in the market.

The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) announced new LPG prices on 4 October. The commission adjusts prices every month. Last month, the official price of a 12kg cylinder was Tk 1,585. For October, it set the maximum retail price at Tk 1,837. However, LPG cylinders are currently being sold in the market for Tk 2,300–2,500.

The LPG Gas Traders Welfare Association sent a letter to BERC on 6 October regarding the sale of LPG at higher prices. The letter said LPG companies issued new price lists from the evening of the day BERC announced the new price.

They set the price of a 12kg cylinder at Tk 1,740–2,000. The association also said it was not possible to sell LPG at the official price because of higher fuel costs, licence fees and other expenses.

In the letter, the LPG Gas Traders Welfare Association said the cost of transporting each cylinder from the company to a distributor’s warehouse is Tk 50. Loading and unloading cylinders from trucks and delivering them to retailers costs another Tk 35.

An additional Tk 25 is required for employee salaries, warehouse rent, electricity bills, licence fees and other expenses. The distributors want a profit of Tk 40 per cylinder.

This means they need Tk 150 per cylinder at the distributor level. They have been receiving a commission of only Tk 50 for the past five years, leaving a shortfall of Tk 100 per cylinder. Meanwhile, differences in prices among companies have created instability in the market.

The association’s letter requested necessary measures to protect the legitimate interests of traders as well as consumers in view of the ongoing instability. The letter, signed by association president Selim Khan, was also sent to the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, the Ministry of Commerce, the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection and the offices of the district commissioners.

BERC, however, says its prescribed wholesale price is Tk 1,742. Distributors receive a commission of Tk 50 per cylinder and are supposed to sell it to retailers for Tk 1,792.

BERC Chairman Jalal Ahmed told Prothom Alo that the commission had received the LPG traders’ association’s letter. However, there is no scope to adjust these costs without a public hearing. The commission will discuss the association’s proposals at its meeting next Sunday and decide what action to take. Until a new decision is made, discussions will be held with traders to ensure they sell LPG at the prescribed price.

BERC has been setting LPG prices since April 2021. At that time, the commission for distributors was set at Tk 50 per cylinder. Distributors are now demanding an increase. However, there have been complaints that LPG is not sold at the official price in the market. Prices often rise sharply in the name of supply shortages. Even after paying higher prices, consumers sometimes cannot obtain LPG.

Tamanna Akhter, a resident of Shewrapara in Mirpur, told Prothom Alo yesterday, Thursday, that a 12kg cylinder was delivered to her home the previous Wednesday and she was charged Tk 2,500—Tk 663 more than the government-set price.

Nationwide drives underway

Nearly 10 million customers use LPG in Bangladesh. About 80 per cent of it is used for household cooking. Demand for LPG began rising sharply after residential gas connections were halted in 2015. Annual LPG demand now exceeds 1.5 million tonnes.

About 99 per cent of the sector is privately operated, with private companies importing and supplying LPG. Besides cooking, LPG is also used in industry and transportation. LPG filling stations for vehicles are also unable to obtain enough LPG to meet demand.

Hasin Parvez, secretary general of the LPG Filling Station Owners Association, told Prothom Alo that a station that requires 30 tonnes a month is receiving only 5–6 tonnes. The stations are facing losses because they cannot sell enough.

LOAB, an organisation of businesses involved in LPG imports and supply, said 158,000 metric tonnes of LPG were imported in August. Another 156,000 tonnes were imported in September. This indicates that imports remain normal, the organisation said. It may take some more time for supply to increase.

LPG distributors say some companies began reducing supplies from 20 September. Meghna Fresh, Omera, iGas, Jamuna, Petromax and BM are mainly supplying LPG to the market. They are selling at prices set by BERC. Several other companies are occasionally supplying very small quantities, but charging higher prices. Some companies have issued price lists showing prices of Tk 1,960–2,000 even though they are not supplying LPG.

The cost of doing business is rising further because distributors are unable to obtain LPG according to demand. They would incur a loss of Tk 150 per cylinder if they sold LPG at the prescribed price.

They say they are therefore being forced to sell at higher prices. At the same time, authorities are conducting drives and imposing fines. The distributors are also considering halting LPG sales if BERC does not accept their demands.

The Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection is conducting nationwide drives to prevent the sale of LPG at inflated prices. Its director Atia Sultana said the agency conducted 242 drives across the country between 2 September and 6 October to monitor the sale of cylinder gas.

A total of 478 distributors and retailers were penalised during the drives. The consumer rights agency fined these establishments a total of Tk 1.125 million. The drives also continued over the past two days.

item.title: Dhaka air 5th worst in world Friday morning
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 5th among the world's most polluted cities on Friday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 172 at 9:15am.
The air quality was classified as ‘unhealthy’, meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Singapore in Singapore ranked first with an AQI score of 217, while Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia ranked second with a score of 210, followed by Lahore in Pakistan in third place with an AQI score of 186.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered 'unhealthy for sensitive groups', while 151 to 200 is classified as 'unhealthy'. A reading between 201 and 300 is considered 'very unhealthy', while levels above 301 are deemed 'hazardous', posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Fired researchers accuse OpenAI of 'chilling' safety efforts
item.description:
Three former OpenAI security researchers on Thursday accused the ChatGPT-maker of firing them for warning about the dangers of artificial intelligence, reigniting the debate over safety at a company whose software has been involved in security breaches.
"I believe we were fired for prioritizing safety over the near-term interests of OpenAI as a corporation," one of the fired staffers, Mikita Balesni, wrote on X, breaking a weeklong silence since their very public dismissal.
Balesni and the two other fired employees, Tomek Korbak and Jasmine Wang, publicly shared a letter to OpenAI on Thursday.
"Our firing leaves us worried that the norms inside OpenAI are shifting," the letter says, and continues that "terminations such as ours, executed and communicated so abruptly, are chilling the open culture OpenAI has prized in the past."
They also call on the company to keep its promise to permanently host independent auditors.
"We are concerned that our firings may be used to justify ending" that work, the letter says.
OpenAI, for its part, said it fired them for allegedly violating company rules.
"Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work," OpenAI told AFP in a statement on October 1.
"We do not terminate employees for raising concerns," a research executive at OpenAI said in a memo to staff on Wednesday, an excerpt of which was shared with AFP.
The three fired researchers worked on monitoring OpenAI's models, which escaped their testing environment in July and hacked Hugging Face, an AI coding library.
The incident sparked a heated debate in Silicon Valley over whether or not to slow the development of this technology.
If OpenAI's researchers can no longer sound the alarm or work with outside parties, "we are all at greater risk that something truly catastrophic will happen," the researchers' letter warns.
They also claim that nearly 400 OpenAI employees signed a petition in July that called for an industry-wide slowdown on advanced development of AI models.
In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX chief Elon Musk called for a slowdown as well.
"Right now we're investing more in safety, security, alignment, monitoring and that will allow us to continue to progress model capability a lot," Altman told reporters last month.
Others, like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, want to move full steam ahead.
US regulators are unlikely to intervene.
Last month, President Donald Trump hosted a group of American tech executives who agreed to abide by a voluntary code of conduct on AI safety.

Nobel winner Pillay jokes about sharing prize with Trump
item.description:
This year's Nobel peace prize winner Navi Pillay joked that she might "share the prize" with US President Donald Trump if people kept applauding her.

"If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump," Pillay said in a video posted to X by the Secretary General of Amnesty International. The video showed Pillay being applauded in Nuremberg after the announcement of the award.

She said that her first reaction to hearing the news was that it must be a joke.

"Being a lawyer and a judge, I still want to verify this," the 85-year-old said, wanting to make sure it was true.

South African judge Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay (85) won the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday "for her efforts to promote peace and international law", the Norwegian Nobel Committee said.

Pillay mentioned her work heading the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which does not speak on behalf of the world body, and which last year found that genocide was occurring in Gaza.

"The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza, naming what's happening there as genocide," she said.

"One of the main reactions to that report is paying tribute to me for my courage. And you can imagine how surprised I was, why would you need courage to speak the truth?" she added.

The prize comes with a gold medal, a diploma and a prize sum of $1.2 million.

The award will be presented at a formal ceremony in Oslo on 10 December, as the day marks the death anniversary of the the prizes' creator, Swedish inventor and philanthropist Alfred Nobel.

Railways cancels trains ahead of 10 October CJP protest, Delhi Police on alert at borders
item.description:
ANI_20261009014

Indian Railways has decided to cancel Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4:00 am and 2:00 pm on 10 October, citing anticipated severe road congestion in the areas around the stations due to a protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi, according to sources.

All Mail and Express trains departing from their originating stations after 2:00 pm on 9 October and scheduled to reach New Delhi or Hazrat Nizamuddin between 4:00 am and 2:00 pm on 10 October will be cancelled at their source stations.

The decision was taken in view of intelligence inputs and traffic advisories indicating severe road congestion around the two railway stations during the period.

Sources said the precautionary measure was aimed at ensuring passenger safety and preventing inconvenience due to traffic congestion.

Separately, West Central Railway’s Bhopal division announced the cancellation of train number 22221 Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (Mumbai)-Hazrat Nizamuddin Rajdhani Express on 9 October due to operational reasons.

In a notice, the railway administration said the train had been cancelled from its originating station. Passengers scheduled to board the train from Bhopal were advised to plan their journeys accordingly and use official railway information and enquiry services for updates.

The railway administration expressed regret for the inconvenience caused to passengers.

Meanwhile, Delhi Police has heightened vigilance at several borders of the national capital ahead of the protest scheduled for 10 October.

Security has been stepped up at the Ghazipur, Chilla, Tikri, Singhu, Gurugram, Kapashera, Loni and Badarpur borders, with police keeping a close watch on movement in these areas.

This comes ahead of the CJP-proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on 10 October over alleged “vote theft”.

However, Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed CJP protest at Jantar Mantar on 10 October over the accountability of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), citing short notice, past non-compliance with directions and concerns related to public safety, law and order and traffic regulation.

Joint Commissioner of Delhi Police Nupur Prasad said an application was received in the New Delhi district on 7 October from Saurabh Das, co-convener of CJP, informing the police about the proposed protest.

“We have received an application from Saurav Das, Co-Convener of Cockroach Janta Party. The application is regarding an intimation for a protest on 10th October at Jantar Mantar. The protest was regarding the accountability of the CEC. This intimation was considered, and it was found that the intimation was given in a very short span of time, whereas as per the prescribed guideline, the intimation has to be received 10 days prior to the protest that is planned. Further, it is also important to mention that on an earlier occasion, when the Cockroach Janta Party was given permission to hold a protest there, they did not follow the lawful directions and did not follow their own undertakings given at that point in time. Therefore, because of not following the legal directions, their own undertaking, and the prevalent law and order situation, and to maintain public safety, law and order, and traffic regulation, this time the permission is rejected; it is not approved,” the Jt CP said.

“It is important to mention that in the New Delhi area, Section 163 of the BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita) is in operation, under which, to maintain public order and safety, a reasonable preventive restriction is in place. It is further important to mention that if anybody violates the provisions of Section 163 of the BNSS, then proper legal action will be taken against them,” she added.

Delhi Police proposes closing 57 metro station gates

Meanwhile, Delhi Police has proposed closing entry and exit gates at 57 metro stations across the national capital and reducing train frequency at these stations in view of proposed protests scheduled for Saturday (10 October), according to an official communication.

In a letter dated Thursday, the Joint Commissioner of Police, Transport Range, requested the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) to take necessary measures at the identified metro stations in view of proposed protests at Jantar Mantar and other locations in New Delhi district, citing the likelihood of unruly crowd movement towards sensitive locations.

The proposed restrictions are scheduled to begin at 9:00 pm on Friday and continue on 10 October until the situation normalises.

The 57 stations identified in the communication include Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, Patel Chowk, Janpath, New Delhi, Mandi House, ITO, Supreme Court, Indraprastha, Kashmere Gate, Karol Bagh, INA, Hauz Khas, Lajpat Nagar, Jamia Millia Islamia, Seelampur, Welcome, Shahdara, Rithala, Rohini East and Rohini West, among others.

The police have requested DMRC to issue necessary directions to its concerned officers and staff to implement the proposed measures.

The communication seeks precautionary arrangements in view of the planned protests. The proposed restrictions are to remain in place until the situation normalises.

The letter says Delhi Police has requested/proposed these measures. It does not, by itself, confirm that DMRC has approved or implemented the closures.

“We will agitate”: CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke says Jantar Mantar protest will go ahead despite no police permission

CJP activist Abhijeet Dipke on Friday reiterated that the organisation would hold a protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on 10 October, despite not receiving permission from Delhi Police.

Dipke asserted that the protest would go ahead regardless of whether police permission was granted and said activists were prepared to face arrest.

Questioning the measures taken ahead of the protest, Dipke said, “What is this fear? Why are you this scared? You are scared of the youth in the country. You shut down trains, you shut down metro, what should one do?”

He also questioned the inconvenience caused to passengers, alleging that restrictions on public transport and roads would themselves cause hardship to ordinary people.

“Is Delhi a property of Narendra Modi or Amit Shah? Is this their ancestral property? Is this their paternal property? On one hand, you say that due to the protest, people are facing inconvenience, and on the other hand, you shut down all the metro, you shut down all the railways, you block all the roads. Now, won’t there be inconvenience for people?” he said.

Dipke said CJP activists were prepared to face detention or arrest over the proposed demonstration.

“How many people will they detain? Arrest me, detain me! Saurabh is ready, Ashutosh is ready. Arrest me, detain me!” he said.

Questioning the need for police permission, he referred to Article 19 of the Constitution and said Jantar Mantar was a designated protest site.

“Did Gyanesh Kumar take permission? Before deleting 13 crore votes, did Gyanesh Kumar take permission? The Supreme Court didn’t even give approval for the Form 6 modification. So, when Gyanesh Kumar, without telling anyone, without asking anyone, deletes 13 crore votes, then to protest against him, the constitutional right we have according to Article 19, what is the need for permission?” he said.

Dipke also questioned the Delhi Police’s statement that applications for protests at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days in advance, linking the restrictions to the proposed demonstration.

“The government is very serious. I think Narendra Modi and Amit Shah should keep checking their blood pressure. The kind of fear this government is showing,” he said.

“Those who don’t vote for BJP have their votes deleted,” says Arvind Kejriwal; urges public to join 10 October protest

Amid strict security preparations across the national capital, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Friday urged the citizens to join upcoming 10 October demonstrations at Jantar Mantar while alleging that under the rule of the BJP and Gyanesh Kumar, votes are being deleted on a mass scale.

Kejriwal stated that the Centre is playing with democracy, while alleging that the BJP deleted the votes of those who did not vote for them and instead added fake votes.

“I appeal to all the people across the entire country that the way the BJP government at the Centre is playing with our democracy, people’s votes are being deleted on a mass scale. Those who don’t vote for the BJP have their votes deleted, while fake votes are added. This was happening openly under Gyanesh Kumar,” Arvind Kejriwal told reporters.

AAP national convenor further urged the citizens to join upcoming demonstrations at Jantar Mantar in maximum numbers and emphasised that this is not about any single individual or party but for the whole country.

He said, “The entire country is demanding Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. I appeal to everyone, all citizens across the nation, to gather in maximum numbers at Jantar Mantar. This is not about any single individual or party; it is about the country.”

AAP convenor confirmed his personal plans to take part Kejriwal and urged others to join as well.

“Protest is beginning at Jantar Mantar. I will be going, my entire family will be going, and I urge all of you to join as well,” Arvind Kejriwal added.

These remarks come after the Delhi Police rejected the application seeking permission for a planned demonstration on 10 October regarding the accountability of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), citing short notice, past non-compliance, and prevailing law-and-order concerns.

SC says no complete ban on Metro services ahead of 10 October protests, asks authorities to regulate movement

The Supreme Court on Friday directed authorities to ensure that metro train services are not completely suspended ahead of the 10 October protests in Delhi, asking the Centre to consider regulated operations of metro and other railway services to prevent inconvenience to commuters.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, while hearing a plea challenging restrictions imposed in the national capital, emphasised the distinction between a complete prohibition on movement and regulating public transport in the interest of law and order.

Recording the assurance given by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, the apex court said the authorities would reconsider the restrictions and allow metro trains and other railway services to operate in a suitably regulated manner, keeping in mind the principle of proportionality.

“...there shall be no complete prohibition on the movement of metro trains,” the top court clarified in its order.

The bench further directed the authorities to ensure that their decision on the regulated movement of metro trains and other railway services receives wide publicity so that commuters are informed in advance and further inconvenience is avoided.

“Such a decision shall be given wide publicity to avoid further inconvenience to commuters,” the apex court said.

During the hearing, the CJI expressed concern over the complete closure of metro station entry gates, pointing out that the restrictions affected thousands of people travelling to Delhi from Gurugram, Greater Noida and other parts of the national capital region for work and education.

The bench observed that students, employees and senior citizens depend on public transport for their daily commute and that security measures should not bring movement to a complete halt.

“Solicitor... we are mainly concerned about the complete closure of these metro station entries. We have serious concerns about this. Our concern is not with respect to any protesters or any individual. Our concern is about the hundreds and thousands of commuters who come from Gurugram, Greater Noida, East Delhi and South Delhi to Delhi for their livelihood. They are students, employees and senior citizens who travel by public transport. We are speaking on behalf of the common citizens of this city,” said the CJI.

“The law enforcement authorities are certainly entitled to take regulatory measures. There is no doubt about that. If you want to restrict unruly movement, you can do so, but that does not mean you can bring everything to a halt and leave people without any transport facility. Everybody does not have a car. Everybody does not have access to private transport. People depend on public transport,” the bench further said.

The apex court stressed that while law enforcement authorities were entitled to regulate movement to maintain law and order, such measures must remain proportionate and take into account the rights and needs of the general public.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta assured the court that he would take its concerns back to the government and that proportionate measures would be considered.

Meanwhile, the bench asked the Centre to take an appropriate decision on reconsidering Jantar Mantar as the designated protest venue and identifying an alternative location, after Solicitor General Tushar Mehta assured it that the government would consider redesignating the protest site.

The top court was hearing the petitions filed by CPI(M) General Secretary MA Baby and other petitioners challenging the curbs imposed by the authorities ahead of the protests.

The apex court’s directions came amid restrictions imposed in Delhi ahead of the proposed 10 October protests. The bench underscored the need to balance security considerations with the public’s ability to access essential transport services.

Senior advocate Kapil Sibal mentioned the matter for urgent hearing regarding the restrictions imposed in Delhi ahead of the 10 October protest called by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Sibal, appearing for Baby, flagged the cancellation of trains to Delhi, closure of metro stations, internet curbs and restrictions on hotel bookings. “What is happening to my country?” he asked.

“All trains have been cancelled, 57 metro stations are shut, people are being denied accommodation in hotels, and Nizamuddin has been closed. RWAs are reportedly being told not to allow people to step out. What is happening to my country? This is a peaceful protest. How can this be allowed to happen?” said Sibal.

item.title: Tanzid provides Bangladesh solid start
item.description:
Riding on a blistering 71-ball 83, Bangladesh kick-started one-off Test against Afghanistan in style, reaching 134-1 at lunch on Day 1 at Sheikh Abu Jayed Stadium in Abu Dhabi, UAE today, Friday.

Tanzid’s marauding start ensured Bangladesh scored runs at six runs per over, keeping the hosts Afghanistan in its adopted venue in UAE in extreme pressure.

But Afghanistan bounced back into the match, thanks to pacer Ismat Alam who dismissed Tanzid, denying him the century on the stroke of lunch.

Tanzid who hammered a century against Australia in Bangladesh’s historical victory in Darwin a couple months ago smashed eight 4’s and four 6’s in his knock.

His swashbuckling knock made his opening partner Shadman Islam a mere spectator. But Shadman came out from the shell after his departure and remained not out on 45 when the lunch was taken.

Mominul Haque was on 5 at the first interval of the day.

Earlier, Bangladesh had opted to bat first after winning the toss. Bangladesh fielded a squad, with an additional spinner in Nayeem Hasan, predicting that the pitch would break considerably after second day to aid the spinners.

item.title: No traffic jams, unusual silence across Mirpur 10
item.description:
The road from Mirpur 10 to Kachukhet in the capital looked markedly different on Friday afternoon following the eviction of street hawkers, with vendors and crowds no longer occupying the footpaths near the Hope International School intersection, leaving the area noticeably quieter.
The change is particularly visible around the Mirpur 10 roundabout and the roads leading towards Kachukhet and Mirpur 1, where hawkers previously occupied footpaths and roadside spaces, contributing to traffic congestion and making movement difficult for pedestrians and vehicles.
Mirpur 10 is one of the busiest areas of the capital. From Farmgate, the road ahead leads towards Mirpur 11, the right turn goes towards Kachukhet, and the left leads towards Mirpur 1.
The roundabout was previously crowded with hawkers, making it difficult for pedestrians to use the footpaths. A similar situation prevailed on the road towards Kachukhet, where roadside vendors occupied the area around Hope International School.
The Mirpur 10 looks quieter following the eviction of street hawkers, with footpaths and roadside spaces cleared of vendors who previously contributed to congestion. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Despite the wide roads, vendors occupied much of the available space, narrowing the passage for vehicles and contributing to traffic congestion. Auto-rickshaws also moved through the narrow stretches, making movement difficult for pedestrians and motorists.
Traffic congestion was common regardless of which direction people traveled from Mirpur 10. That scene has now changed, with roadside shops absent from the roundabout and surrounding areas and the usual noise having subsided.
The roads are now noticeably quieter, with no traffic jams.
Hope International School, located on the road towards Kachukhet, was previously surrounded by roadside vendors. Although the road was wide, more than half of it was occupied by roadside businesses, reducing the space available for vehicles and contributing to traffic congestion.
The roadside shops and hawkers are now absent, making the full width of the road visible. The same change can be seen on the road branching off to the left near Hope International School, where roadside shops are no longer present on either side.
The road near Hope International School in Mirpur is seen free of roadside shops following the eviction of street hawkers, restoring space for pedestrians and vehicles. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Local resident Abdul Hamid said: “Previously, it was impossible to walk on this road. Hawkers and auto-rickshaws occupied the space so heavily that vehicles could not move properly. After the hawkers were evicted, we were surprised to see how wide the road actually was. Now children can walk comfortably, and we can move around freely too.”
Another resident, Abul Kashem, said: “It is difficult to describe how the hawkers had occupied these areas. People were also fed up with the occupation of footpaths and extortion. Now these problems are no longer there. It feels good.”
He said he hoped the situation would continue so residents could live peacefully. If the areas were occupied again, he added, unrest would return. Residents wanted the roads and footpaths to remain clear permanently, he said.
From the Mirpur 10 roundabout towards Mirpur 1, including the area beyond the stadium, no hawkers can be seen. With shops no longer occupying the footpaths, pedestrians and motorists can see the full width of the roads.
Local resident Selim Mia said: “It is surprising to think about how Mirpur 10 used to be and how it is now. Where people could not walk before, the entire road is now clear.”
He said similar initiatives were needed to make Dhaka livable, adding that people occupying roads to set up shops should be evicted and the roads kept open for public movement.
Abir Hossain said the city corporation had taken a very good initiative. Previously, movement was difficult from morning until midnight, but the situation had changed, he said. Schoolchildren can now walk to school comfortably, and the earlier traffic jams are no longer there. Overall, he said, the area now offers a much better environment.
On September 30, the Mirpur 10 roundabout area turned into a battleground amid vandalism, arson and repeated clashes between police and hawkers during a footpath eviction drive.
During the operation, a fire at a shop triggered repeated chases and counter-chases between police and hawkers, turning the area into a scene of confrontation. The situation came under control in the afternoon. The opposition leader and the Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) administrator visited the scene.
File photo of fire breaks out at Hope Market during a clash between hawkers and police amid an eviction drive in Mirpur-10. Photo: Abir Ahmmed Shupto/Dhaka Tribune
Eyewitnesses said an electrical wire snapped during the eviction drive, causing a short circuit and a fire that destroyed 6–7 shops beneath Baitul Quddus Jame Mosque near the Mirpur 10 roundabout.
Angered by the incident, hawkers and traders began vandalizing property. At one point, hawkers set fire to 3 city corporation garbage trucks and vandalized an excavator.
Police fired tear gas to bring the situation under control, while protesters threw bricks and stones at police.
Journalists, police personnel, city corporation workers, traders and others were injured in the incident.

item.title: South African judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize
item.description:
The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded Friday to South Africa’s Navi Pillay, the judge who headed the Rwanda genocide tribunal and who last year presided over a UN commission which accused Israel of genocide in Gaza.
Pillay, currently a judge on the International Court of Justice in a case where Myanmar also stands accused of genocide, has been “instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide are prosecuted,” said Jorgen Watne Frydnes, the chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee in Oslo.
Pillay headed the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which does not speak on behalf of the world body, and which last year found that genocide was occurring in Gaza.
Pillay told AFP at the time that her team had shared “thousands of pieces of information” with prosecutors at the International Criminal Court.
The UN said the prize for Pillay was testimony to the “value” of rights.
The Nobel jury said it was honoring her at a time when “the system of international law is under tremendous pressure and its institutions are under attack.”
“At a time of existential challenges -- including more wars and conflicts than the world has seen in a long time -- international law is no longer just a supplement to peace and security. It is an absolute necessity,” Watnes said.
“Navi Pillay’s commitment to universal legal principles and her firm moral compass are constants in a long career,” the committee said.
The prize -- the ultimate diplomatic and humanitarian accolade -- is sure to irk US President Donald Trump, whose administration has repeatedly attacked international justice institutions.
Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prize.
“If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump,” Pillay said to a standing ovation captured by Amnesty International Secretary General Agnes Callamard in Nuremberg and posted on the social network X.
Last year, the prize went to Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, who subsequently gave her Nobel gold medal to Trump.
The prize comes with a gold medal, a diploma and a prize sum of $1.2 million.
The award will be presented at a formal ceremony in Oslo on December 10, the anniversary of the 1896 death of the prizes’ creator, Swedish inventor and philanthropist Alfred Nobel.
The Peace Prize is the only Nobel awarded in Oslo, with the other disciplines announced in Stockholm.
On Thursday, the Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to Canadian poet Anne Carson for her modern twists on Greek mythology and antiquity that have inspired new forms of writing.
The 2026 Nobel season winds up Monday with the economics prize.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,147 as three die in 24 hours
item.description:
Three more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Friday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,147.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all three of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,043, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
The three new suspected fatalities were reported across three divisions; Sylhet, Chittagong, and Barisal with one death each.
A total of 1,268 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Friday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 202,893.
During the same period, 81 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 22,197.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 180,079 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 172,705 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.
